title: Polymer-Encapsulated Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Platforms for Fabricating Magnetic Soft Materials

properties.summary: The unencapsulated cluster shows a decrease in χMT on cooling, attributed to antiferromagnetic interactions and zero-field splitting.

source_locations.location: Figure 1 and discussion of the previously determined crystal structure

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The previously crystallographically characterized cluster cation has a reported diameter of 2.8 nm and serves as the inorganic core of the polymer-encapsulated materials.

synthesis.procedure: S-1 sulfonate-terminated poly(ethylene glycol) monoalkyl ether was mixed with the Gd52Ni56 cluster in water; PEC-1 was obtained as a green precipitate. The main article gives no numerical reagent quantity.

reagents.name: S-1 sulfonate-terminated poly(ethylene glycol) monoalkyl ether

synthesis.time: Cluster solution added dropwise over 30 min; stirred for 30 min; stood for 10 min

properties.summary: The polymer shell partly reduces intercluster antiferromagnetic interactions. Its UV–visible spectrum retains characteristic absorption bands of the cluster core.

measurements.name: UV–visible absorption bands
measurements.conditions: Characteristic bands of the Gd52Ni56 cluster core in the PEC spectrum

source_locations.location: UV–visible discussion (Figure S5); Figure 4 and magnetic-susceptibility discussion

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The Gd52Ni56 cation is electrostatically encapsulated by S-1 polymer sulfonates; elemental analysis indicates approximately 17 sulfonate anions per cluster cation. Individual PEC-1 units coexist with self-assembled unilamellar vesicles in dichloromethane.

synthesis.procedure: S-2 sulfonate-terminated poly(ethylene glycol) monoalkyl ether was mixed with the Gd52Ni56 cluster in water; PEC-2 was obtained as a green precipitate. The main article gives no numerical reagent quantity.

reagents.name: S-2 sulfonate-terminated poly(ethylene glycol) monoalkyl ether

synthesis.time: As in the PEC-1 procedure: 30 min dropwise addition, 30 min stirring, then 10 min standing

properties.summary: Its longer polymer shell effectively shields intercluster antiferromagnetic interactions; its magnetic-susceptibility curve nearly overlaps that of PEC-3. The UV–visible spectrum retains cluster-core absorption bands.

measurements.name: UV–visible absorption bands
measurements.conditions: Characteristic bands of the Gd52Ni56 cluster core in the PEC spectrum

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The Gd52Ni56 cation is electrostatically encapsulated by S-2 polymer sulfonates; elemental analysis indicates approximately 19 sulfonate anions per cluster cation. Individual units and unilamellar vesicles occur in dichloromethane, while solid-state SAXS indicates lamellar assembly.

synthesis.procedure: S-3 sulfonate-terminated poly(ethylene glycol) monoalkyl ether was mixed with the Gd52Ni56 cluster in water. The water-soluble mixture was dialyzed against water to remove sodium nitrate formed by ion exchange. The main article gives no numerical reagent quantity.

reagents.name: S-3 sulfonate-terminated poly(ethylene glycol) monoalkyl ether

synthesis.time: 30 min dropwise addition, 2 h stirring, then 24 h dialysis
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Aqueous mixing, electrostatic association, and dialysis
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Dialyzed against water to remove sodium nitrate

properties.summary: Its longer polymer shell effectively shields intercluster antiferromagnetic interactions. PEC-3 is water-soluble and was demonstrated as an in vivo MRI contrast agent, enhancing tumor MR signal after intratumor injection. Its UV–visible spectrum retains cluster-core absorption bands.
